The [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"), officially known as the Games of the XXXIII Olympiad, were an international multi-sport event held in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), France, from 26 July to 11 August 2024, with preliminary events in some sports beginning on 24 July.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-3) Athletes representing 206 [National Olympic Committees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") (NOCs) participated in the games.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-4) The games featured 329 medal events across 32 [sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_sports "Olympic sports") and 48 disciplines.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-5) [Breaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaking_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Breaking at the 2024 Summer Olympics") ([breakdancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakdancing "Breakdancing")) made its Olympic debut as an optional sport, while [skateboarding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skateboarding_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Skateboarding at the 2024 Summer Olympics"), [sport climbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_climbing_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Sport climbing at the 2024 Summer Olympics"), and [surfing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surfing_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Surfing at the 2024 Summer Olympics") returned to the programme, having debuted at the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-7)

The [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "United States at the 2024 Summer Olympics") led the final medal table for the fourth consecutive Summer Games, with 40 gold and 126 total medals, while [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "China at the 2024 Summer Olympics") finished second with 40 gold and 91 medals in total.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-17) The occasion marked the first time a gold medal tie among the two most successful nations has occurred in Summer Olympics history.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-18) Among individual participants, Chinese swimmer [Zhang Yufei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Yufei_\(swimmer\) "Zhang Yufei \(swimmer\)") won the most medals at the games with six (one silver, five bronze),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-19) while [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "France at the 2024 Summer Olympics") swimmer [Léon Marchand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9on_Marchand "Léon Marchand") had the most gold medals with four.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-20)
## Medals
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Medals")]
See also: [Olympic medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal "Olympic medal")
[Paris 2024 Organizing Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Organising_Committee_for_the_2024_Olympic_and_Paralympic_Games "Paris Organising Committee for the 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games") President Tony Estanguet unveiled the [Olympic and Paralympic medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal "Olympic medal") for the Games in February 2024, which on the obverse featured embedded hexagon-shaped tokens of scrap iron that had been taken from the original construction of the [Eiffel Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower "Eiffel Tower"), with the Games' logo engraved into it.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-21) Approximately 5,084 medals were produced by the French [mint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mint_\(facility\) "Mint \(facility\)") [Monnaie de Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monnaie_de_Paris "Monnaie de Paris"), and designed by [Chaumet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaumet "Chaumet"), a luxury jewellery firm based in Paris.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-22)
The reverse of the medals featured [Nike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike_\(mythology\) "Nike \(mythology\)"), the Greek goddess of victory, inside the [Panathenaic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panathenaic_Stadium "Panathenaic Stadium") which hosted the [first modern Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Summer_Olympics "1896 Summer Olympics") in 1896. The Parthenon and the Eiffel Tower could also be seen in the background on both sides of the medal.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-23) Each medal weighed 455–529 g (16–19 oz), had a diameter of 85 mm (3.3 in) and was 9.2 mm (0.36 in) thick.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-24) The gold medals were made with 98.8 percent silver and 1.13 percent gold, while the bronze medals were made up with copper, zinc, and tin.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-25)

The medal table is based on information provided by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [Olympic medal table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal_table "Olympic medal table") sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-The_Independent-8)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-27) If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [IOC country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_IOC_country_codes "List of IOC country codes").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-28)
Events in [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Boxing at the 2024 Summer Olympics") result in a bronze medal being awarded to each of the two competitors who lose their semi-final matches, as opposed to fighting in a [third place tiebreaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_place_playoff "Third place playoff").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-29) Other combat sports, which include [judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Judo at the 2024 Summer Olympics"), [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Taekwondo at the 2024 Summer Olympics"), and [wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Wrestling at the 2024 Summer Olympics"), use a [repechage system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repechage_system "Repechage system") which also results in two bronze medals being awarded.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-30)
